newsitem.title: USA: Bank profits soar on stock rally, restructurings.
newsitem.headline: Bank profits soar on stock rally, restructurings.

text.p: Banks reported outstanding fourth-quarter profits Monday as Wall Street firms benefitted from the stock and bond market rallies while mergers or restructurings helped several regional banks.

J.P. Morgan & Co. Inc.'s profits rose a surprisingly strong 14 percent to $419 million from $366 million in the year-ago period. Earnings per share grew to $2.04 from $1.80, far more than the Wall Street consensus estimate of $1.69.
Revenues grew to $1.81 billion from $1.52 billion.

"Our business grew substantially in 1996 and produced strong results across the range of our advisory, capital raising, asset management, risk management and trading activities," said Chairman Douglas Warner III.

Trading revenues rose 39 percent to $512 million, and investment banking revenues rose 75 percent to $277 million as the Wall Street firm took on higher levels of advisory, syndication and underwriting activities.
"Trading came up very good; investment banking was stronger than my estimates," said Denise Petsis, analyst at Nomura Securities. "It's definitely a revenue growth story here."
Securities Data Corp. ranked J.P. Morgan the sixth-largest underwriter of U.S. debt and stock issues and fifth-largest adviser in completed mergers and acquisitions worldwide in 1996.
Investment management fees rose 17 percent to $182 million mainly as a result of net new business.
Operating expenses rose 21 percent to $1.197 billion as compensation grew in line with improved earnings and costs rose with increased activity in client businesses.
Barnett Banks Inc., the largest banking company in Florida, was among several in the industry that had record fourth-quarter and full-year 1996 profits.
Barnett reported record fourth-quarter profits of $149.8 million, or 76 cents a share, up 13 percent from $138.3 million, or 67 cents a share, a year earlier.

Full-year 1996 earnings also grew 12 percent to a record $564.5 million, or $2.86 a share, from $533.3 million, or $2.56 a share, in 1995. The results included a $24.5 million charge in the third quarter to cover a special assessment to recapitalize the Savings Association Insurance Fund.

"Our product line continues to expand and we are offering more ways for customers to access us anywhere, anytime," said Charles Rice, chief executive of the Jacksonville, Fla.-based bank. "Barnett's culture is changing from a traditional bank to a financial services organisation."
NationsBank Corp., based in Charlotte, N.C., said its profits rose to $632 million, or $2.19 a share, in the quarter ended Dec. 31, from $510 million, or $1.87 a share, in the 1995 period.

Operating profits for the full-year 1996 surged 26 percent to $2.45 billion, or $8.26 a share, from $1.95 billion, or $7.13 a share, in 1995, before a charge mainly related to the merger with Bank South.

National City Corp., based in Cleveland, also had record fourth-quarter earnings of $191.1 million, or 85 cents a share, up 48 percent from $129.1 million, or 57 cents a share, for the year-ago period.
Full-year net income rose 24.5 percent to a record $736.6 million, or $3.27 a share, from $591.5 million, or $2.64 a share, in 1995.

SouthTrust Corp., which has 511 offices in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina and Tennessee, saw fourth-quarter earnings jump 28 percent to $68.4 million from $53.6 million in the 1995 period. Earnings per share rose 16 percent to 71 cents from 61 cents.
The Birmingham, Ala.-based company's full-year 1996 net income shot up 28 percent to $254.7 million, or $2.69 a share, from $199.0 million, or $2.36 a share, in 1995.
Synovus Financial Corp., based in Columbus, Ga., said its earnings rose to $41.7 million, or 36 cents a share, in the fourth quarter, from $33.6 million, or 29 cents a share, in 1995 period.
